name: Cape Town Globus Data Path
description: Globus Connect Server endpoints at FIU or CIEN whose data traffic to the SANReN Cape Town DTN runs over an L2 facility-port VLAN, while Globus reaches them on public addresses.
description_long: Demonstrates that Globus data can be steered onto a private research path purely by where the endpoints advertise their data interface. Each DTN VM (Rocky 9, one slice per run at the SITE chosen: FIU or CIEN; run it twice with the same prefix for both) gets a public uplink (AmLight-Layer3-FIU at FIU, FABnetv4Ext at CIEN) on which Globus Connect Server 5.4 is registered, and a data NIC bridged through an L2 facility port (AmLight-EXP-Layer2-FIU at FIU, FP2-CIEN at CIEN) onto the VLAN that reaches the Cape Town DTN; that NIC is GCS's --data-interface. FABRIC offers only VLANs 4000-4094 on AmLight-EXP-Layer2-FIU, so the weave takes a free one and reports it for the operators to map to Cape Town's VLAN 1400 on the switch. The Cape Town side runs Globus Connect Personal, which opens every data connection itself to the advertised address, so the bytes take the VLAN - for transfers submitted from the CLI or the web app alike. The weave checks the address is not already in use, reachability and jumbo frames to Cape Town, the public addresses (no NAT), firewalls the public NIC to 443 + 50000-51000, creates one mapped collection per endpoint, saves each deployment key under results/keys, writes results/legs.json and exits. globus_transfer_demo.ipynb runs transfers to and from the Cape Town collection and proves the path from the DTN's own sockets. Stop deletes each Globus endpoint before its slice, and keeps the slice if that fails.

args.name: SLICE_NAME
args.label: Slice name prefix
args.description: Prefix for the slices: <prefix>-fiu, <prefix>-cien

args.name: SITE
args.label: Site
args.description: Where to build the DTN: FIU or CIEN (CIEN is offline for now). Slice <prefix>-fiu or <prefix>-cien. The network fields below are blank = this site's default (shown greyed out). For both DTNs, run the weave twice with the same prefix, once per site.

args.name: FP_BW
args.label: Facility port bandwidth (Gbps)
args.description: Bandwidth reserved on every facility port (above the project limit needs Net.NoLimitBW)

args.name: PUBLIC
args.label: Public uplink
args.description: How Globus reaches the DTN: an L3 facility port name, or 'ext' = FABNetv4Ext.

args.name: PUBLIC_VLAN
args.label: Public VLAN
args.description: VLAN on the public facility port (auto = first free). Ignored for 'ext'.

args.name: PUBLIC_ADDR
args.label: Public IPv4 address
args.description: IPv4 CIDR on the public facility port (assigned by the facility). Ignored for 'ext'.

args.name: PUBLIC_GW
args.label: Public IPv4 gateway
args.placeholder: first usable address of the subnet
args.description: Blank = the first usable address of PUBLIC_ADDR's subnet.

args.name: PUBLIC_ADDR6
args.label: Public IPv6 address
args.description: IPv6 CIDR on the public facility port (blank at CIEN = IPv4 only).

args.name: PUBLIC_GW6
args.label: Public IPv6 gateway
args.description: Blank = the first usable address of PUBLIC_ADDR6's prefix.

args.name: L2_FP
args.label: Data facility port
args.description: L2 facility port toward the Cape Town DTN.

args.name: L2_VLAN
args.label: Data VLAN
args.description: VLAN on the data port (auto = first free). At FIU the operators map it to Cape Town's VLAN 1400.

args.name: L2_IP
args.label: DTN data address
args.description: This DTN's address on the Cape Town VLAN.

args.name: PEER_IP
args.label: Cape Town data address
args.description: The Cape Town DTN's address on the same VLAN.

args.name: HOST
args.label: Worker host
args.description: Pin the VM to a worker (blank = FABRIC picks).

args.name: GLOBUS_USERS
args.label: Globus users
args.description: Globus identities allowed to use the collections, comma-separated: identity or identity=account, e.g. you@unc.edu (account = the part before @) or you@renci.org=komal. Each account is created on the DTN with <dir>/<account>.

args.name: GLOBUS_CONTACT_EMAIL
args.label: Globus contact email
args.description: Contact shown on the endpoints

args.name: GLOBUS_ORG
args.label: Globus organization
args.description: Organization shown on the endpoints

args.name: GLOBUS_DISPLAY_NAME
args.label: Endpoint name
args.description: The site is appended: '... (FIU)'. Never rename a live endpoint - a new name makes a second collection.

args.name: GLOBUS_CLIENT_ID
args.label: Globus service client ID
args.description: Client UUID of a Globus Connect Server service credential (app.globus.org > Settings > Developers > your project > Add a service credential). With the secret, the weave saves it in this weave (globus_creds.env, mode 0600, never printed) and later runs reuse it.

args.name: GLOBUS_CLIENT_SECRET
args.label: Globus service client secret
args.description: The secret shown once when the credential is created. Only needed on the first run (or to replace the credential); leave blank afterwards.

args.name: GLOBUS_ADMIN
args.label: Globus administrator
args.description: Globus identity granted the administrator role on each endpoint (needs a Globus subscription; blank = none)

args.name: GLOBUS_PROJECT_ID
args.label: Globus Auth project
args.description: UUID of the Globus Auth project the endpoints are registered in: app.globus.org > Settings > Developers > your project > Project ID. Use the project that holds the service credential above. Blank works when the credential belongs to only one project; set it if endpoint setup asks for --project-id.

args.name: DATA_BASE
args.label: Collection directory
args.description: Directory on the DTN published as the mapped collection; each mapped user gets <dir>/<account>

args.name: CAPE_COLLECTION
args.label: Cape Town collection
args.description: Globus collection on the Cape Town DTN (SANReN GCP - Cape Town SC26)

args.name: DEMO_UI
args.label: Demo web UI
args.description: Install the demo web UI on each DTN (127.0.0.1 only; reach it with the SSH tunnel command the weave prints)

args.name: DEMO_UI_PORT
args.label: Demo UI port
args.description: Port of the demo web UI on the DTN and on your end of the tunnel

args.name: GLOBUS_NATIVE_CLIENT_ID
args.label: Globus native app client
args.description: Native-app client used to sign in from the demo UI / notebook (default: Globus SDK tutorial client; register your own for anything long-lived)

args.name: DATA_PATH
args.label: Globus data path
args.description: vlan = GCS advertises the Cape Town VLAN address for data (the demo); public = advertise the public uplink, so transfers with Cape Town work before the VLAN is mapped (also switchable live from the demo UI)

args.name: DATA_MTU
args.label: Data MTU
args.description: MTU on the data NIC; drops to 1500 automatically if jumbo frames do not reach Cape Town

args.name: DATA_NIC
args.label: Data NIC
args.description: NIC_Basic | NIC_ConnectX_5 | NIC_ConnectX_6 (FIU has ConnectX-5)

args.name: CORES
args.label: Cores
args.description: DTN VM cores

args.name: RAM
args.label: RAM (GB)
args.description: DTN VM memory (GCS needs 8+)

args.name: DISK
args.label: Disk (GB)
args.description: DTN VM disk; the collection lives on it

args.name: LEASE_DAYS
args.label: Lease (days)
args.description: Every slice is renewed to this many days

args.name: KEEP_SLICE
args.label: Keep slices
args.description: true = Stop / cleanup never delete anything. false = cleanup removes each Globus endpoint, then its DTN slice.

args.name: FORCE_DELETE
args.label: Force delete
args.description: Stop/cleanup: delete a DTN slice even if removing its Globus endpoint failed (remove it at app.globus.org first)
